Local Surrogate Explanation for Survival Predictions (LIME-style)

Source: R/compute_surrogate.R
compute_surrogate.Rd

Builds a sparse, locally weighted linear surrogate model to explain a fitted survival model's prediction at a specific target time for a single instance. Categorical features are binarized relative to the instance of interest; local weights are computed from feature-space proximity (Gower by default); and a penalized (lasso) or unpenalized linear model is fit to approximate the model's predicted survival probability at target_time.

Usage

compute_surrogate(
  model,
  newdata,
  baseline_data,
  times,
  target_time,
  k = 5,
  dist.fun = "gower",
  gower.power = 5,
  kernel.width = NULL,
  penalized = TRUE,
  exclude = NULL
)

Arguments

model

An mlsurv_model fitted via fit_*(), containing a valid $learner so that predict_<learner> can be dispatched.

newdata

A one-row data frame: the instance to explain (must have the same predictors as baseline_data).

baseline_data

A data frame used to define the local neighborhood and to fit the surrogate (typically the model's training data).

times

Numeric vector of times passed to the prediction function; must include target_time (nearest value is used).

target_time

Numeric time at which to explain the prediction.

k

Desired number of non-zero coefficients for the penalized surrogate (used only when penalized = TRUE); acts as a target sparsity.

dist.fun

Distance function for locality weighting. Default "gower" (via gower); otherwise any method accepted by dist (requires kernel.width).

gower.power

Power applied to \((1 - \text{gower\_dist})\) when dist.fun = "gower" to control locality sharpness (default 5).

kernel.width

Positive numeric bandwidth used for non-Gower kernels (Gaussian weighting on pairwise distances).

penalized

Logical; if TRUE (default) fits a lasso surrogate via glmnet; otherwise fits a weighted least squares lm().

exclude

Optional character vector of column names to exclude from the surrogate (in addition to survival outcome columns).

Value

A data frame with one row per selected feature containing:

feature

Feature name (after recoding).

feature_value

Value of the feature in newdata.

effect

Local contribution \(\beta_j \cdot x_j\) at target_time.

target_time

The explanation time (copied for plotting).

Rows are ordered by decreasing \(|effect|\).

Details

Target: The surrogate approximates \(S(t^{*} \mid x)\) returned by the underlying model at target_time. The nearest column in times is used.

Weights: Locality weights are computed from distances between baseline_data rows and newdata. With "gower", weights are \((1 - \mathrm{gower\_dist})^{\mathrm{gower.power}}\); otherwise Gaussian \(\exp\{-d^2 / \mathrm{kernel.width}^2\}^{1/2}\).

Sparsity: When penalized=TRUE, a glmnet path is fit and the solution with degrees of freedom closest to k is selected (preferring exactly k if available).

Examples

# \donttest{
mod <- fit_coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, data = veteran)
local_expl <- compute_surrogate(
  model = mod,
  newdata = veteran[2, , drop = FALSE],
  baseline_data = veteran,
  times = c(80, 160),
  target_time = 80,
  k = 3
)
head(local_expl)
#>    feature feature_value     effect target_time
#> 1    karno            70 0.65901926          80
#> 2 celltype      squamous 0.18321600          80
#> 3      age            64 0.04473744          80
# }
